children: Global investment bank JPMorgan reiterates its 'Overweight' rating on Reliance Industries on November 19, retaining its price target of Rs 1,675

Promoter entities of Reliance Industries (RIL) have acquired a combined 14.27 lakh shares worth approximately Rs 194 crore through market transactions conducted on November 16 and November 18, according to disclosures filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The purchases were made by Reliance Services and Holdings and Reliance Industrial Investments and Holdings, with both entities buying shares on each of the two trading days.

On November 18, each entity acquired five lakh shares valued at Rs 68.29 crore. Following the transactions, Reliance Services and Holdings' stake increased to 34.40 crore shares, while Reliance Industrial Investments and Holdings' holding rose to 48.21 crore shares.

The earlier acquisitions took place on November 16. Reliance Services and Holdings purchased 2.15 lakh shares worth Rs 28.81 crore, taking its holding to 34.38 crore shares. Reliance Industrial Investments and Holdings bought another 2.12 lakh shares valued at Rs 28.34 crore, increasing its stake to 48.19 crore shares.
All four transactions were categorised as promoter acquisitions of equity shares in the NSE disclosures.
As of the end of the September quarter of FY27, the promoter and promoter group collectively held 6,71,54,96,096 shares, representing 50.44 per cent of RIL's paid-up equity capital.

The promoter purchases come after Reliance Industries reported record financial performance for the second quarter of FY27. Consolidated net profit rose 33.8 per cent year on year to Rs 29,550 crore, while revenue increased 27.8 per cent to an all-time high of Rs 3.62 lakh crore.

Consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) climbed 23.9 per cent to a record Rs 62,409 crore. Profit before tax advanced 32.6 per cent to Rs 38,613 crore. The company's first-half profit also crossed Rs 50,000 crore for the first time.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) division delivered record earnings, while digital services continued to expand. The retail business, however, faced margin pressure from inflation, with a shift in the festive calendar also influencing the year-on-year comparison.

Global investment bank JPMorgan reiterated its 'Overweight' rating on Reliance Industries on November 19, retaining its price target of Rs 1,675. The target implied an upside of around 23 per cent from the stock's closing price of Rs 1,363 on Wednesday.
The brokerage identified an earnings recovery and supportive valuations as key factors underpinning its positive outlook.

Analyst positioning on the stock remains favourable, with all 33 analysts covering Reliance Industries maintaining a 'Buy' recommendation. Their consensus price targets suggest an upside potential of approximately 16 per cent from prevailing levels.
Despite the positive brokerage outlook and promoter purchases, RIL shares ended lower on the BSE. The stock settled at Rs 1,352.50, declining Rs 22.60, or 1.64 per cent, during the session.
